summary: Equal trees force any correct comparison to inspect every corresponding node. The paired recursive traversal performs exactly that linear work and keeps only one root-to-leaf path on the call stack.

optimality.argument: For two equal n-node trees, changing the value or presence of the last unexamined node would change the answer. A correct algorithm must therefore inspect all n corresponding positions in the worst case, giving Omega(n) time. The candidate compares each corresponding node pair once and recurses only into matching child directions, so it uses O(n) time and O(h) stack space.

replacement_checks.evidence: An equal-tree input cannot be distinguished from a last-position value or structure mismatch without examining every corresponding node.
Each corresponding node pair is visited at most once, while the recursion retains at most one path of height h.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover equality, a structural mismatch, and a value mismatch; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
